videos.description:
How to Find Any Building Permit Office & Permit Portal on ConstructHUB - a building permit office lookup that gives you the official permit portal of a county or city, or says plainly when none is on record.
A directory of county and city permit offices in all 50 states and DC.

Made for contractors: roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing, electrical and general contractors.
Try ConstructHUB: https://constructhub.us

IN THIS VIDEO
• The Database Directory
• Search by city, county or state
• No portal on record: a web search, never a guessed link
• Permits issued by Hillsborough County
• Clear filters to browse
• Filter by state

STEP BY STEP
1. The Database Directory - This is the Database Directory. It lists county and city permit offices in all fifty states and Washington, D.C.
2. The totals: jurisdictions, portals on record, through their county - The numbers at the top show how many jurisdictions are listed, how many have a permit portal on record, and how many get their permits through their county.
3. Search by city, county or state - To find a place, type a city, county or state in the search box. Let's look for Tampa.
4. Verified portal: the link is on record and was checked - Tampa, Florida says Verified portal. Its official permit portal is on record, and the link has been checked.
5. Open portal goes to the city's permit portal - Open portal takes you to the city's permit portal, in a new tab.
6. No portal on record: a web search, never a guessed link - Tampa, Kansas has no portal on record. Instead of a guessed link, you get Find permit portal, a web search for that town's permit portal.
7. Some towns get their permits from the county - Some towns don't issue their own permits. Search for Apollo Beach.
8. Permits issued by Hillsborough County - Its row says permits are issued by Hillsborough County, and gives you a button for the county's permit portal.
9. The source link shows where that comes from - The Source link opens the official page that information comes from.
10. Property lookup opens Property Records for the same county - Property lookup opens Property Records, filtered to the same county.
11. Clear filters to browse - Choose Clear filters to browse instead.
12. Counties or Cities - Counties shows only counties, and Cities shows only cities and towns.
13. Filter by state - Pick a state to narrow the list. We'll choose Florida.
14. Then by county - A second menu then lets you choose a single county.
15. Menu: Permits & Databases, Database Directory - You'll find the Database Directory in the menu, under Permits and Databases. It's free to browse.

WHAT YOU NEED
• Free to browse.

GOOD TO KNOW
Lists each jurisdiction with its official permit portal link when one is on record and has been checked. Links that could not be confirmed are labelled, and where no portal is known you get a "Find permit portal" web search instead of a guessed link.
Portal links are stored only after a liveness check, and dead ones are marked. Nothing in the directory is generated or guessed.

THE SHORT VERSION, FROM THE IN-APP HELP
1. Sidebar → Permits & Databases → Database Directory.
2. Find the county or city you need.
3. Open its official portal link, or use "Find permit portal" when there is none.

WHY CONTRACTORS USE IT
Some towns do not issue their own permits, and the directory says so and points to the county that does. Property Records is the companion page: a finder for the official county property appraiser or assessor office.

videos.description:
How to create and send an estimate in ConstructHUB CRM - construction estimating with a price book, line items and a private link the client approves and signs.
A short walkthrough of writing an estimate in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will pick a client, add work from the price book, set the quantity, review the total and send it. Then you will open the preview to see what the client sees before they approve.

Made for contractors: roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing, electrical and general contractors.
Try ConstructHUB: https://constructhub.us

IN THIS VIDEO
• Start a new estimate: Estimates; New estimate; Step 1: pick the client; Dana Whitfield
• Add work from the price book: Step 2: search the price book; Add the item; Quantity; Price and wording can be changed
• Review and send: Review; Step 3: title; Check the total; Send estimate
• Preview what the client sees: Open this estimate; Sent, opened, valid until; Preview; The client's view

CHAPTERS
0:00 Start a new estimate
0:15 Add work from the price book
0:31 Review and send
0:48 Preview what the client sees

STEP BY STEP
▶ Start a new estimate
1. Let's write an estimate and send it to a client. Start on the Estimates page.
2. Choose New estimate.
3. Step one is the client. Search by name, email or phone.
4. We'll pick Dana Whitfield.
▶ Add work from the price book
5. Step two is the work. Search your price book for an item.
6. Choose Add. The item comes in with its price and its scope of work.
7. Set the quantity. This kitchen needs thirty square feet, and the total updates.
8. You can change the price and the wording for this job.
▶ Review and send
9. When everything is in, choose Review.
10. Give the estimate a title your client will recognise.
11. Check the lines and the total.
12. Then choose Send estimate. The client gets an email with a private link.
13. The estimate now has a number, and it's marked as sent.
▶ Preview what the client sees
14. Open it to see how it's doing.
15. This line shows when it was sent, and whether the client has opened it yet.
16. Preview shows you the client's view, in a new tab.
17. This is what your client sees after confirming their email. They approve the estimate by typing their full name.
18. Your company details are at the top, then the work and the total.
19. Back in the CRM, the estimate waits for the client's answer.
20. You'll find Estimates in the menu on the left.
The client names, jobs and figures on screen are sample data in a demo workspace.

WHAT YOU NEED
• A ConstructHub CRM plan - the CRM is a separate product with its own plans.
• Price book items to pick from.
• An email address on the client, to send to.

GOOD TO KNOW
The three-step way to write a bid and get it in front of a client: pick the client, add the work from your price book, review and send.
Each price book item you add brings its price and its scope of work; you set the quantity and can change the price or the wording for this job. Sending emails the client a private link to the estimate and marks it Sent. "Save as draft" keeps it without sending.
The client opens the link, confirms their email with a one-time code, and approves by typing their full name. Preview opens the same page for you with approving and paying switched off, and it does not count as the client opening it.

THE SHORT VERSION, FROM THE IN-APP HELP
1. CRM → Estimates → New estimate, then search for the client or choose New client.
2. Search your price book, choose Add on each item, and set the quantity.
3. Choose Review, give the estimate a title, and check the total.
4. Choose Send estimate. Preview on the estimate's page shows what the client sees.

WHY CONTRACTORS USE THIS
A client who re-opens a bid is a cue to call, and the estimate shows when it was opened. Change a price once in the price book and every new estimate uses it.

How to set up your profile in ConstructHUB CRM - contractor team management: invite the crew, set roles, and put your company details on every document.
A short walkthrough of My profile in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will set your name, title and mobile number, see your role, and save. Then you will see how to open your profile again from the menu.

Whether you run a roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing, electrical or general contracting business, the steps are the same.
Try ConstructHUB: https://constructhub.us

IN THIS VIDEO
• My profile: Team & Company; My profile tab
• Name, title and mobile: Name; Title; Mobile; Role
• Save your profile: Save profile; Profile saved; Your name opens it; Saved details

CHAPTERS
0:00 My profile
0:10 Name, title and mobile
0:27 Save your profile

STEP BY STEP
▶ My profile
1. Team & Company - Your profile is how you appear to your crew and on the schedule. Let's set it up.
2. My profile tab - On Team and Company, the first tab is My profile.
▶ Name, title and mobile
3. Name - Name is what your crew sees next to your jobs and visits.
4. Title - Title is your job at the company. Type it the way you want it shown.
5. Mobile - Mobile is your own cell number. We'll type a demo number here.
6. Role - Role shows what you may do in the CRM. You can't change your own role here.
▶ Save your profile
7. Save profile - When it looks right, choose Save profile.
8. Profile saved - The CRM says Profile saved, and takes you back to Home.
9. Your name opens it - To change it later, click your name at the bottom of the menu.
10. Saved details - Your title is saved, and the mobile number is stored with its country code.
11. Menu: Team & Company - You'll also find My profile under Team and Company in the menu.
Everything on screen - names, addresses, prices - is sample data from a demo workspace.

WHAT YOU NEED
• A ConstructHub CRM plan - the CRM is a separate product with its own plans.

GOOD TO KNOW
Your own name, title and mobile number in the CRM - how you appear to your crew and on the schedule.
My profile holds your name, your title and your mobile number, and shows the role you have. Save profile stores them and takes you back to Home.
Your role is shown here but is not changed here: roles are set on the Team tab. Saving a mobile number does not sign you up for text alerts - those are switched on separately, in Settings → Notifications.

THE SHORT VERSION, FROM THE IN-APP HELP
1. CRM → Team & Company → My profile, or click your name at the bottom of the menu.
2. Check your name, then type your title and your mobile number.
3. Choose Save profile.

WHY CONTRACTORS USE THIS
Divisions give one company separate operating arms, each with its own name, address and license. The company details kept here are the ones that print on your documents. A pending invite can be resent or cancelled, and a member's role can be changed later. People are invited by email with a role - Owner, Admin, Sales, Project manager, Office, Field or Subcontractor. The role decides what a person can see and change, and the server enforces it. Individual permissions can be adjusted when one person needs a little more or less than their role gives. Removing someone cuts their access immediately, and what they created stays.

videos.description:
How to report an issue from the CRM in ConstructHUB CRM - contractor CRM integrations: a website lead form, calendar feeds, online payments, API keys and webhooks.
A short walkthrough of Report an issue in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will say what you were trying to do and what happened, pick how bad it is, and send the report. Then you will see where its status and our reply appear.

Made for contractors: roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing, electrical and general contractors.

IN THIS VIDEO

• Describe the problem: What were you trying to do?; What happened instead?; No passwords; Which page?
• Send it and follow it: Send report; Report number; Your reports; Bottom of every page

CHAPTERS
0:00 Open Report an issue
0:10 Describe the problem
0:39 Send it and follow it

STEP BY STEP
▶ Open Report an issue
1. Any CRM page - When something in the CRM doesn't work, you can tell us from the page you are on.
2. Report an issue - At the bottom of the page, choose Report an issue.
▶ Describe the problem
3. What were you trying to do? - First, say what you were trying to do.
4. What happened instead? - Then say what happened instead: what you clicked, and what you saw.
5. No passwords - Leave out passwords and card numbers. We never need them.
6. Which page? - Which page is filled in from where you came from. Change it if the problem is somewhere else.
7. How bad is it? - Pick how bad it is. A report that says you can't use the site is looked at first.
8. Screenshot - You can add one screenshot. It's optional.
▶ Send it and follow it
9. Send report - Then choose Send report.
10. Report number - You get a report number, and the issue desk reads every report.
11. Your reports - Your reports shows its status. Our reply appears here too.
12. Bottom of every page - You'll find Report an issue at the bottom of every CRM page.
Everything on screen - names, addresses, prices - is sample data from a demo workspace.

WHAT YOU NEED
• A ConstructHub CRM plan - the CRM is a separate product with its own plans.

GOOD TO KNOW
The form for telling ConstructHUB that something in the CRM is not working, without leaving the CRM.
You say what you were trying to do, what happened instead, which page it was on and how bad it is, and can attach one screenshot. Sending it gives you a report number, and the report is listed under "Your reports" with its status and our reply.
The page, your browser, your window size and the time are sent with the report so the problem can be reproduced; "What we send with your report" lists them before you send. Reports that stop you from working are looked at first.

THE SHORT VERSION, FROM THE IN-APP HELP
1. At the bottom of any CRM page, choose Report an issue.
2. Fill in what you were trying to do and what happened instead. Leave out passwords and card numbers.
3. Check "Which page?" - it is filled in from the page you came from - and pick how bad it is.
4. Choose Send report, then follow it under "Your reports".

WHY CONTRACTORS USE THIS
A measurement report lands on the client whose address matches it. Online payments run through your own connected Stripe account. A lead-capture form goes on your own website by embed code or link, and what people send becomes clients tagged as website leads. Each integration is set up once, from its own card on the Integrations page. Read-only API keys and webhooks let your own systems read from the CRM and be told when something happens. An API key is shown in full only once, when it is created, so it cannot be read back out of the page later.

videos.description:
Tour the price book: items, materials, labor in ConstructHUB CRM - contractor estimate software that builds a bid from your price book and sends it for e-signature.
A short tour of the price book in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will see the four tabs - Price Chart, Materials, Labor and Formulas - search for an item, and preview a quantity to see its material, labor, total, cost and margin.

Made for contractors: roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing, electrical and general contractors.
Try ConstructHUB: https://constructhub.us

IN THIS VIDEO
• The Price Chart: The price book; Four tabs; A SKU: name, code, unit, description; Add SKU and From template
• Check a price: Type a quantity; Preview; Material, labor, total; Cost and margin
• Materials and labor: Materials; Margin per material; Labor; The default rate
• Formulas: Test; The answer; Menu: Price book

CHAPTERS
0:00 The Price Chart
0:23 Check a price
0:38 Materials and labor
0:54 Formulas

STEP BY STEP
▶ The Price Chart
1. This is your price book. It's the price list your estimates pick from.
2. It has four tabs: Price Chart, Materials, Labor and Formulas.
3. Price Chart lists what you sell. Each item has a name, a code, a unit and a description.
4. Add SKU and From template bring in new items.
5. To find an item, search by name or code.
▶ Check a price
6. To check a price, type a quantity. Here it's one hundred twenty feet of baseboard.
7. Then choose Preview.
8. The item expands into its material and its labor, with waste added, and a total.
9. The last line shows your cost and your margin.
▶ Materials and labor

How to set team roles and permissions in ConstructHUB CRM - contractor team management: invite the crew, set roles, and put your company details on every document.
A short walkthrough of roles and permissions in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will read what a role is for, change a team member's role, and switch one permission on for one person.

For roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors, and general contractors who run their own office.
Try ConstructHUB: https://constructhub.us

IN THIS VIDEO
• Roles on the Team tab: Team tab; Team members; Owen Brooks
• What a role is for: The i beside a role; Role: Project manager; Close
• Change a role or one permission: Change a role; Team member updated; One permission; Still a project manager

CHAPTERS
0:00 Roles on the Team tab
0:14 What a role is for
0:26 Change a role or one permission

STEP BY STEP
▶ Roles on the Team tab
1. Roles decide what each person on your team can see and do. Here is how to set them.
2. On the Team tab, under Team members, everyone has a role.
3. Owen is a project manager. The switches show what he can do.
▶ What a role is for
4. Click the i beside a role to read what it's for.
5. A project manager runs jobs once they're sold. The back office stays with owners and admins.
6. Press Escape to close it.
▶ Change a role or one permission
7. To change a role, pick a new one from the list. We'll make Priya office staff.
8. The CRM says Team member updated, and her role is now office.
9. You can also change one thing for one person. Let's let Owen see costs and margins.
10. The switch is on, and Owen is still a project manager.
11. The owner has every permission, and that can't be changed here.
12. You'll find roles under Team and Company in the menu.
The recording uses a demo workspace: the people, jobs and amounts in it are sample data.

WHAT YOU NEED
• A ConstructHub CRM plan - the CRM is a separate product with its own plans.
• Owner or admin access to manage the team.

GOOD TO KNOW
The role each person on your team has, and the switches that say what that person may see and do.
Every team member has a role - owner, admin, sales, pm (project manager), office, field or subcontractor - and a row of permission switches that start from that role. The "i" beside a role explains what it is for. You can change a person's role, or flip one switch for one person.
Roles set the defaults; a switch you flip overrides the role for that person only. The owner has every permission and cannot be changed here. The server checks the permission on every request, so a switch that is off is off everywhere.

THE SHORT VERSION, FROM THE IN-APP HELP
1. CRM → Team & Company → Team, and scroll to Team members.
2. Click the "i" beside a role to read what that role is for.
3. Pick a different role from the list to change it.
4. Flip a single switch to allow or stop one thing for that one person.

WHY CONTRACTORS USE THIS
Removing someone cuts their access immediately, and what they created stays. Divisions give one company separate operating arms, each with its own name, address and license. The company details kept here are the ones that print on your documents. A pending invite can be resent or cancelled, and a member's role can be changed later. The role decides what a person can see and change, and the server enforces it. Individual permissions can be adjusted when one person needs a little more or less than their role gives.

A short walkthrough of adding an item to the price book in the ConstructHUB CRM. You will name the item, pick its unit, set a price and an optional cost, write the scope of work, save it, and preview a quantity.

For roofing, siding, remodeling, flooring, painting, HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors, and general contractors who run their own office.

STEP BY STEP
▶ Open Add SKU
1. Let's add a new item to your price book.
2. Choose Add SKU.
3. Give the item a name your crew and your clients will recognise.
4. Leave Code empty, and the item gets the next SKU number.
▶ Unit and price
5. Pick the unit you sell it by. Crown molding is priced per linear foot.
6. Pricing mode stays on Flat price: one price for each unit.
7. Type the price for one unit.
8. Cost is optional. It's what the item costs you.
▶ Scope and save

The Add SKU form: one item in your price book, with its unit, its price and the scope of work your client reads.

The scope of work shows on every estimate built from the item, with its line breaks kept. The pencil on an item opens the same form to change it.

5. Search for the item, type a quantity and choose Preview to check the total.

A price book turns estimating into picking from a menu: each item brings its price and its scope of work, so bids stay consistent from one job to the next. The client gets an email with a private link where they can read the bid, ask a question, approve and e-sign - nothing to print. Each estimate carries a status - Draft, Sent, Viewed, Approved, Declined or Expired - so you can see where every bid stands. A client who re-opens a bid is a cue to call, and the estimate shows when it was opened.
